Alphabet — key metrics, Q2’26

GOOGL · USD · series 2026-09-22T01:52:56Z · built 2026-09-24 13:27 UTC

The short version

Alphabet’s Q2’26 does not print a Search break: Search & other revenue re-accelerated to $63.3B (+16.8% YoY) while paid clicks rose +13% and CPC cooled to +3%. Cloud is strong and secondary at $24.8B (+81.8%). Quarterly free cash flow flipped to −$5.8B as capex overtakes. The stock trades at 17.29× trailing earnings (price asof 2026-09-16); the official street forward prints sit at 16.23× (FY1) and 22.47× (FY2).

Long-only, 3–10 year horizon. The primary falsifiers are a sustained Search / front-door loss and an ad-moat / RPM break — structural ad weakness without an AI monetization path. Secondary: Cloud or YouTube share loss, or a Waymo stall. Cloud is on the scoreboard, but it is not the thesis.

Search — re-acceleration, not a front-door collapse

Search dollars grew +16.8% in Q2’26 to $63.3B. The YoY path ran roughly +12–14% through 2024, dipped toward ~10% in early 2025, then stepped up to ~14.5% in Q3’25, ~19.1% in Q1’26 and +16.8% now. That is re-acceleration in the dollar line, not a sustained loss of the front door.

What the file cannot see is the product surface itself: there is no Gemini MAU, query-share, or AI Overviews monetization series in the cabinet. Search dollars plus clicks/CPC are the observable proxies, and they currently argue against the collapse print.

Monetization quality — clicks up, price cooled

The sharper falsifier lens is monetization quality. 2024 was a high-CPC / soft-click year — CPC often +7–8% with clicks at +4–6%. Into 2026 the pattern flipped: clicks +13% in both Q1 and Q2 while CPC cooled to +5%, then +3%. Volume is carrying the Search line while price growth fades.

That is the live ad-moat / RPM question — not a Search revenue collapse. If AI-assisted queries monetize worse than classic commercial intent, it shows up here first.

Ads stack — still Search-heavy, Network is the soft line

The ads stack summed to $81.6B in Q2’26 (+14.4%). Search’s share of ads drifted up to ~77.5% from 76.0% a year ago, while Network — the third-party line — slipped to ~8.9% of ads from ~10.3%. YouTube ads printed $11.1B (+12.9%): healthy, and a secondary watch rather than the primary falsifier.

Network is the clearer soft product line in revenue terms: $7.30B, −0.7% YoY. Impressions fell −12% while CPI rose +13% — price is covering volume loss on the third-party side.

Geography is context, not a falsifier axis: Q2’26 revenue split Americas $67.9B, EMEA $32.5B, APAC $19.3B, with the mix drifting slowly international.

TAC — no blow-up, with one flagged pair of years

Traffic acquisition cost was $16.2B in Q2’26, +10% YoY. The disclosed TAC/ads rate is ~19.8%, down from ~20.6% a year earlier — distribution costs are not eating the ads business.

One audit flag stays on the page: FY2022 and FY2023 annual TAC both store $48.955B — identical dollars with different disclosed rates (22.0% vs 21.4%). Until the MD&A bind is audited, those two FY dollar prints are not load-bearing. FY2025 TAC was $59.9B at a 20.3% rate.

Cloud — strong, and deliberately second on the page

Cloud revenue reached $24.8B (+81.8% YoY) with operating income of $8.81B at a 35.6% margin — against $2.83B at 20.7% a year ago. It is the growth and margin-expansion story in the file.

It is also secondary to the thesis locks: the falsifiers live in Search and ads, so Cloud sits here, after them, on purpose.

P&L and cash — OI is the trajectory; capex has overtaken FCF

Quarterly revenue was $119.8B (+24.2% YoY) with operating income of $40.8B (+30.4%) — a 34.0% operating margin versus ~32.4% a year ago and ~36.1% in Q1’26. Margin is firm-to-up even with the AI build-out.

Net income of $112.2B is not a clean run-rate: the release ties a very large one-time tax/securities item (~$99B class) into the NI and EPS jump. Operating income is the operating trajectory; the raw NI margin is treated as distorted.

The cash quarter tells the capex story directly: operating cash flow of $39.1B against $44.9B of capex leaves FCF at −$5.8B — the first clear quarterly deficit in the window. Q1’26 still printed +$10.1B.

Annual grain keeps the context: FY2025 free cash flow was $73.3B on $91.4B of capex. The quarterly deficit is new; the full-year machine is still heavily cash-positive.

  • TAC FY2022 / FY2023 store identical dollars ($48.955B) with different rates — audit pending.
  • Waymo operating KPIs (trips, paid miles, markets) are absent — Other Bets revenue and OI alone cannot score the optionality.

Out of scope

This pack does not score the contrarian, EU-DMA, or antitrust remedy digs — those live on their own pages. It does not invent weekly trailing history before mid-2024, an NTM print, or Waymo KPIs; it does not chart the flagged FY2022/FY2023 TAC dollars without the twin flag; and it does not let Cloud bury Search.

Method & definitional notes
  • Diluted weighted-average shares are sparse (9 of 44 periods, starting 2024-06-30), so pe_ttm / pe_fy are null before mid-2024 — PE history starts mid-2024 by construction.
  • pe_ttm prints only on complete trailing-four-quarter net income with diluted WAS and a USD close. The latest (17.29 at FY2026Q2) uses the $342.94 close asof 2026-09-16 — not the 2026-06-30 period-end close.
  • pe_fy is FY-end only (FY2024 23.54, FY2025 28.97) and is never labeled TTM.
  • Weekly trailing PE ships as complete ISO weeks only (n_sessions ≥ 4, Sunday before asof ET), priced on the volume-weighted average of daily closes (not true trade VWAP); diluted-WAS sparsity starts the series at 2024-W26 — nothing earlier is invented. Latest W37 (week_end 2026-09-13): weekly_price 334.43, weekly_pe_ttm 16.86 — USD/USD, labeled separately from the period pe_ttm 17.29 (later close asof 2026-09-16) and never blended with it.
  • Q2’26 net income ($112.2B) includes a large one-time tax/securities item; the TTM net income behind pe_ttm ($244.21B) inherits it. Use operating income for the operating trajectory.
  • TAC FY2022 and FY2023 both store $48.955B (identical) while disclosed rates differ (22.0% vs 21.4%) — twin-dollar audit pending; do not lean on those two FY dollar prints.
  • Network revenue is not TAC — Network is the third-party ads revenue line; TAC is traffic acquisition cost.
  • Forward PE is the single official W37 street print (Yahoo GAAP EPS asof 2026-09-17 over the W37 weekly price 334.43 — volume-weighted average of daily closes, not true trade VWAP). NTM is null; FY2 (22.47) > FY1 (16.23) because street FY2 EPS ($14.88) < FY1 ($20.61) — a curiosity, not a signal.
  • Income Q4 quarters (10 rows, FY2016Q4–FY2025Q4) are FY − Q1−Q2−Q3 residuals (extract_method=residual in the source CSV) — usable for trajectory, not new accession facts.
  • Waymo / Other Bets operating KPIs (trips, paid miles, markets) are absent — Other Bets revenue and OI only; optionality is not scoreboardable yet.
  • No Gemini / AI Overviews engagement or query-share series exists in the file — Search revenue plus clicks/CPC are the observable front-door proxies.
  • Product / segment / monetization / geo series are quarters only (FY stubs excluded upstream; Q1–Q3 per year). Cash and TAC carry explicit quarter / ytd / annual windows and are never mixed on one axis.
